mainTopic: ברכות on borderline foods (ground-baked dough, date honey, crushed dates, שתיתא) and the wording ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ versus ״מוֹצִיא״
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about חלה, then turns to the ברכות on borderline foods. רב יוסף rules that כּוּבָּא דְאַרְעָא, dough baked in the ground, is only kneaded dough and gets בורא מיני מזונות. However, מר זוטרא made a full meal on it and said המוציא and ברכת המזון. מר בר רב אשי adds that such bread counts as לחם עוני for מצה on פסח. He also rules that date honey gets שהכל, because it is only moisture from the fruit, following רבי יהושע's view on fruit juices of תרומה. In contrast, crushed dates (טרימא) keep בורא פרי העץ because they are still the fruit. רב and שמואל argue about שתיתא, and רב חסדא explains that thick שתיתא is food and gets מזונות, while thin שתיתא is medicine and gets שהכל. A challenge from the laws of שבת leads to the rule that anything a person enjoys needs a ברכה, even when he eats it for health. Finally, the גמרא explains the dispute between the חכמים (״הַמּוֹצִיא״) and רבי נחמיה (״מוֹצִיא״) and begins a story about רבי זירא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ruling on thick versus board-shaped dough for חלה
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a ברייתא: dough shaped thick like loaves must have חלה taken, and dough shaped flat like boards is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made them thick, they are obligated in חלה. If he made them like boards, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of a ברייתא quoted on the previous page. These are its final words about when dough becomes obligated in חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shape shows what the dough is meant for. Thick pieces look like loaves of bread, so they are treated as bread and need חלה. Flat, board-like pieces will clearly be used only as an ingredient in כותח (a dip), so they are exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the tail end of a ברייתא that started on the previous page, so do not read it as a stand-alone ruling with no subject.

phrases.english: If he made them thick — they are obligated,
phrases.notes: Thick pieces look like bread, so they are obligated in חלה.

phrases.english: If like boards — they are exempt.
phrases.notes: Flat pieces are clearly meant for כותח, not for eating as bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dough shaped like loaves is obligated in חלה. Dough shaped like boards, meant for כותח, is exempt.

steps.title: אביי asks which ברכה to say on ground-baked dough
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף which ברכה is said over כּוּבָּא דְאַרְעָא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: This dough baked in the ground — what ברכה do we say over it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. אביי asks his teacher רב יוסף which ברכה to say on a kind of dough baked in a pit in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question arises because this food sits on the border. It looks something like bread, but it is not baked in a normal oven. So it is unclear whether it gets המוציא, like bread, or the ברכה for other grain foods.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough baked in a hole in the ground

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
This dough of the ground (baked in the earth)
phrases.notes: Dough baked in a pit dug into the ground, not in a regular oven.

phrases.english: What blessing do we recite over it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about ברכות on borderline grain foods.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether כובא דארעא gets המוציא, like bread, or בורא מיני מזונות.

steps.title: רב יוסף answers: it is only kneaded dough, so the ברכה is מזונות
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says it is not real bread, only kneaded dough, so one says בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think it is bread? It is just kneaded dough, and we say over it 'בורא מיני מזונות'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי. This food does not count as bread, so its ברכה is בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף says it does not have the status of bread at all. It is only a mass of kneaded dough. So it gets the ברכה for grain foods that are not bread, not המוציא.

keyTerms.meaning: Kneaded dough, a lump of dough
The ברכה over grain foods that are not bread

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי סָבְרַתְּ נַהֲמָא הוּא?!
phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think it is bread?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: of course it is not real bread.

phrases.english: It is merely kneaded dough
And we recite over it: 'Who creates various kinds of nourishment.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי סָבְרַתְּ נַהֲמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כובא דארעא is only kneaded dough, not bread, so its ברכה is בורא מיני מזונות.

steps.title: מר זוטרא made a meal on it and said המוציא
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא made this dough the basis of his meal. He said המוציא before eating and the three blessings of ברכת המזון after.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא made his meal on it. He said 'המוציא לחם מן הארץ' over it and afterward the three blessings of ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what מר זוטרא actually did. When he made this dough the main food of a full meal, he treated it like real bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new detail to רב יוסף's rule. Eaten casually, it is just dough and gets מזונות. Once a person makes a full meal on it (קביעות סעודה), it is treated as bread and gets המוציא and full ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it the basis of his meal (קביעות סעודה)
The three blessings of ברכת המזון

steps.confusionAlert: מר זוטרא does not disagree with רב יוסף. רב יוסף is talking about eating it casually. מר זוטרא is talking about making a whole meal on it, and that changes its status.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the well-known rule that grain foods normally getting מזונות, such as פת הבאה בכיסנין, become המוציא when a person makes a full meal on them.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra based his meal on it,
and recited over it: 'Who brings forth bread from the earth,'
and the three blessings (of Grace after Meals).
phrases.notes: Full ברכת המזון afterward, as for real bread.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Limitation of רב יוסף's ruling (practice of an אמורא)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to רב יוסף's ruling for when a full meal is made on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one makes a full meal on כובא דארעא, it is treated as bread: המוציא before and ברכת המזון after.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: such bread can be used for מצה on פסח
steps.stepSummary: A person can fulfill his מצה obligation on פסח with these breads, because they are called 'לחם עוני'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: A person fulfills his obligation on פסח with them. Why? Because we call it 'bread of affliction'.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי adds a ruling about the same kind of simple dough. It can be used to fulfill the מצה obligation on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls מצה 'לחם עוני', poor man's bread. Plain, simple dough like this fits that description exactly. So for פסח purposes it counts as bread, even though casually it only gets מזונות.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread of affliction or poverty, the תורה's name for מצה
We call it, we apply the term to it

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: And a person fulfills his obligation with them on Passover,
phrases.notes: 'Them' refers to these simple breads, such as כובא דארעא.

phrases.english: What is the reason? We call it 'bread of affliction.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of dough to a different law, מצה on פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One fulfills the מצה obligation with these simple breads, because they count as לחם עוני.

steps.title: The ברכה on date honey is שהכל
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי rules that date honey gets שהכל, because it is only moisture oozing from the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And מר בר רב אשי said: Over this date honey we say 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'. Why? It is just moisture.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי moves to a related ברכות question. He rules that date honey gets שהכל, not בורא פרי העץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dates themselves get בורא פרי העץ. The honey, however, is not considered the fruit itself, only liquid that seeps out of it. Since it is not the essence of the fruit, it gets the general ברכה of שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: The general ברכה: by Whose word all came to be
Sweat, moisture, the liquid that seeps out

steps.whatToRemember: Grain dough eaten casually gets מזונות, but becomes bread (המוציא and ברכת המזון) when a full meal is made on it, and it counts as לחם עוני for מצה. Date honey is only moisture from the fruit, so it gets שהכל and not בורא פרי העץ.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the principle that liquids coming out of fruit, other than wine and olive oil, generally lose the fruit's ברכה and get שהכל.

phrases.english: And Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
This date honey
we recite over it: 'By Whose word all things came to be.'
What is the reason? It is merely moisture.
phrases.notes: It is not the fruit itself, only liquid that drips out of the fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַאי דּוּבְשָׁא דְתַמְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling by the same אמורא, on a new food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Date honey gets שהכל because it is only moisture seeping from the fruit, not the fruit itself.

steps.title: Whose opinion supports the date honey ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier authority מר בר רב אשי's ruling follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier source agrees with מר בר רב אשי that date honey gets only שהכל. This one-word question sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר רב אשי said date honey is only 'moisture' coming out of the fruit and not the fruit itself. The גמרא wants a תנא who also treats fruit juice as separate from the fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? This asks which authority a ruling follows.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
phrases.notes: This refers back to מר בר רב אשי's ruling in Step 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source behind Step 6's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that fruit juice does not have the status of the fruit itself?

steps.title: רבי יהושע's view on fruit juices of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The ruling follows רבי יהושע, who exempts a non-כהן who drinks fruit juice of תרומה from paying קרן וחומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows this תנא, as we learned in a משנה: date honey, apple wine, vinegar from late-season grapes, and other fruit juices of תרומה. רבי אליעזר obligates the principal plus a fifth, and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מר בר רב אשי follows רבי יהושע. In this משנה, רבי יהושע exempts someone who drank fruit juices of תרומה from the usual penalty payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-כהן who eats תרומה by mistake must normally pay back the value plus an extra fifth (קרן וחומש). רבי יהושע exempts him for juices because he does not see juice as real fruit. The same idea explains why date honey loses בורא פרי העץ and gets only שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: Date honey, the syrup that oozes out of dates.
The portion of produce given to a כהן. A non-כהן may not eat it.
The principal plus an extra fifth, the payment due from a non-כהן who ate תרומה by mistake.
Late-season, stunted grapes that are not good for making wine.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא linking a law of ברכות to a law of תרומה. Both rest on the same question: is juice still considered 'the fruit'?

phrases.english: Like this Tanna, as we learned in a Mishnah:
Date honey, and apple wine,
and vinegar made from late-season grapes,
and other fruit juices of terumah:
Rabbi Eliezer obligates the principal plus a fifth,
phrases.notes: He holds that juice counts as the fruit itself.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts.
phrases.notes: He holds that juice is only a byproduct. מר בר רב אשי follows this view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מר בר רב אשי follows רבי יהושע, who treats fruit juice as less than the fruit itself.

steps.title: A student asks רבא about טרימא
steps.stepSummary: A student asks רבא what the law is for טרימא, but רבא does not understand the word.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages said to רבא: What is the law of טרימא? רבא did not understand what he was saying to him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins: a student asks רבא about something called טרימא. רבא does not recognize the word, so the story continues in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new topic, though it is still about processed fruit. Steps 10-11 work out what the word means, and Step 13 gives the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Crushed or pounded food. Here it turns out to mean crushed dates.
What is it? What is the law?

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to Rava:
What is the law of terima?
It was not clear to Rava's mind
what he was saying to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְרָבָא טְרִימָא מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about another kind of processed fruit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ברכה is said over טרימא?

steps.title: רבינא asks which kind of טרימא is meant
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks the student which kind of crushed food he means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא was sitting before רבא. He said to the student: Do you mean sesame? Or safflower? Or grape pits?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tries to help by asking the student to explain his question. He lists three possible things that are crushed this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a clarifying question, not a challenge. The word טרימא was too general, and רבינא is narrowing down what food the student is asking about.

phrases.english: Ravina was sitting before Rava,
he said to him: Are you speaking of sesame,
or are you speaking of safflower,
or are you speaking of grape pits?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to clarify the unclear word from Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which food is the student calling טרימא?

steps.title: רבא understands: crushed food
steps.stepSummary: רבא figures out that the student means crushed food, here crushed dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, רבא understood. He said to him: You are surely speaking of crushed food.
steps.whatsHappening: While רבינא was talking, רבא worked out what the word means. He tells the student he must be asking about crushed food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case is defined: food that is pounded but not turned into liquid. As the next steps show, the case is about dates.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile; in the time this was happening.

phrases.english: Meanwhile,
Rava brought it up to his mind (understood),

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲשִׁילְתָּא וַדַּאי קָא אָמְרַתְּ,
phrases.english: he said to him: You are surely speaking of crushed food,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the meaning of the word the student asked about.

steps.title: רב אסי: טרימא may be made from תרומה dates, but not beer
steps.stepSummary: רבא recalls רב אסי's ruling: you may make טרימא from dates of תרומה, but you may not make beer from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you reminded me of what רב אסי said: Dates of תרומה may be made into טרימא, but they may not be made into beer.
steps.whatsHappening: The question reminds רבא of a ruling by רב אסי about dates of תרומה. Crushing them is allowed, but brewing them into beer is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may not ruin תרומה. Crushing keeps the dates intact as food, so it is allowed. Brewing beer destroys the fruit, so it is forbidden. This shows that טרימא is still treated as the fruit itself.

keyTerms.meaning: And you reminded us of a matter.

phrases.english: And you reminded us of a matter,
that which Rav Asi said:
These dates of terumah,
it is permitted to make terima from them,
phrases.notes: The fruit stays whole in substance.

phrases.english: and it is forbidden to make beer from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַדְכַּרְתַּן מִלְּתָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ruling that shows טרימא keeps the fruit's status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dates of תרומה may be made into טרימא but not into beer, because beer destroys the fruit.

steps.title: The הלכה: crushed dates get בורא פרי העץ
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that dates made into טרימא keep the ברכה בורא פרי העץ, because they stay in their original state.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: over dates that were made into טרימא, one says בורא פרי העץ. Why? Because they remain as they were at first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules on the student's original question. Crushed dates still get בורא פרי העץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Date honey (Step 6) is only liquid that oozed out, so it gets שהכל. Crushed dates are still the actual fruit, only mashed. So they keep the fruit's ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is; the final practical ruling.
The ברכה said on fruit that grows on trees.

steps.whatToRemember: Date honey, which is only liquid, gets שהכל. Crushed dates (טרימא) keep בורא פרי העץ because the fruit itself is still there.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up טרימא with date honey. Both come from dates, but only the honey has lost the fruit's identity.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a practical rule: mashing a fruit does not change its ברכה, as long as the fruit's substance remains.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: dates that were made into terima,
one blesses over them 'Who creates fruit of the tree.'
What is the reason?
They stay in their state, as they were originally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on the question from Step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Crushed dates keep בורא פרי העץ because they are still the original fruit.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about שתיתא
steps.stepSummary: About שתיתא, רב says שהכל and שמואל says בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: שתיתא: רב said 'שהכל נהיה בדברו', and שמואל said 'בורא מיני מזונות'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new food, שתיתא (a drink or mix made from roasted barley flour), and records a מחלוקת about its ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treats שתיתא as a general food that gets שהכל. שמואל looks at the grain inside it and gives it מזונות. The next part of the גמרא will explain this disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: A mix of roasted barley flour with honey or vinegar.
By Whose word all things came to be; the general ברכה.
Who creates various kinds of nourishment; the ברכה on grain foods.

phrases.english: Shetita (a roasted barley-flour mix):
Rav said: 'By Whose word all things came to be,'
and Shmuel said: 'Who creates various kinds of nourishment.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case of a processed food and its ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: שתיתא gets שהכל. שמואל: שתיתא gets בורא מיני מזונות.

steps.title: רב חסדא: thick versus thin
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that רב and שמואל do not really argue. שמואל is talking about thick שתיתא, and רב is talking about thin שתיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: They do not really disagree. One is talking about a thick mixture, and the other about a thin one. A thick mixture is made to be eaten as food. A thin mixture is made to be used as medicine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא resolves the argument from step 14 by showing that רב and שמואל are each talking about a different kind of שתיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thick שתיתא is made as real food, so it gets the grain ברכה, בורא מיני מזונות, which is שמואל's ruling. Thin שתיתא is made as medicine, so it only gets שהכל, which is רב's ruling. The deciding factor is why the person made it: for eating or for healing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: the purpose a food was made for can change its ברכה. The next step challenges this exact idea.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: And they do not disagree:
This is about a thick one, this is about a thin one.
phrases.notes: שמואל's ruling is about thick; Rav's is about thin.

phrases.english: A thick one, they make it for eating,
a thin one, they make it for medicine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the argument between רב and שמואל from step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case (אוקימתא): each opinion applies to a different kind of mixture
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and שמואל seem to disagree about the same food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thick שתיתא gets בורא מיני מזונות. Thin שתיתא gets שהכל.

steps.title: רב יוסף challenges from the laws of שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא that allows mixing שתיתא on שבת. If שתיתא were medicine, that should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף raised a challenge: A teaching says everyone agrees that you may mix שתיתא on שבת and drink Egyptian beer. But if you think the person means it as medicine, is medicine allowed on שבת?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב חסדא's claim that thin שתיתא is made for healing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis forbade taking medicine on שבת. Yet the ברייתא allows mixing שתיתא on שבת. This suggests that שתיתא is not treated as medicine at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a challenge from an earlier teaching
Egyptian beer, a drink people took for healing

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether mixing counts as forbidden work on שבת. The question is only about the rabbinic ban on taking medicine on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised a challenge:
And they agree that one may mix shetita on Shabbat
and may drink Egyptian beer.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לִרְפוּאָה קָא מְכַוֵּין,
phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that he intends it for medicine,
is medicine permitted on Shabbat?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea in step 15 that thin שתיתא is medicine
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that thin שתיתא is made for healing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Medicine is forbidden on שבת. A ברייתא allows שתיתא on שבת. So שתיתא must not be considered medicine.

steps.title: אביי: food eaten for healing is allowed on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a משנה: you may eat and drink ordinary foods on שבת even for healing. This is because the person counts as someone who is eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Don't you agree with this too? We learned in a משנה: A person may eat any food for healing on שבת, and may drink any drink. What must you say to explain that? The person is treated as intending to eat. Here too, the person is treated as intending to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף by pointing to a משנה that רב יוסף must also accept. That משנה answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on medicine on שבת applies only to things that are clearly medicine. Ordinary foods may be eaten even when the goal is healing, because it just looks like normal eating. שתיתא is an ordinary food, so mixing it on שבת is allowed even if the person wants it for healing. So רב חסדא's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְאַתְּ לָא תִּסְבְּרָא?
phrases.english: Abaye said to him: And don't you hold this?
But we learned in a Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָאוֹכָלִין אוֹכֵל אָדָם לִרְפוּאָה בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: All foods, a person may eat for healing on Shabbat,
and all drinks, he may drink.
Rather, what must you say?
The man intends to eat,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי גַּבְרָא לַאֲכִילָה קָא מְכַוֵּין.
phrases.english: so too here, the man intends to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְאַתְּ לָא תִּסְבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge from step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a parallel משנה that רב יוסף must also accept
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything done for healing is forbidden on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ordinary food eaten for healing counts as eating, so it is allowed on שבת.

steps.title: Another version: healing just happens by itself
steps.stepSummary: A second version of אביי's answer: the person means to eat, and the healing comes on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: What must you say? The person intends to eat, and the healing happens by itself. Here too, he intends to eat, and the healing happens by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a slightly different wording of אביי's answer from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version said the person is simply treated as eating. This version admits there is a healing effect but says it is only a side result, not the person's goal. Either way, שתיתא is allowed on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Ordinary food stays allowed on שבת even when it heals. Either the person counts as eating, or the healing is just a side effect.

phrases.english: Another version:
Rather, what must you say?
The man intends to eat,
and the healing comes about by itself?
So too here, he intends to eat,
and the healing comes about by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second wording of אביי's answer in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Healing as a side effect of eating
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any healing benefit would make the food forbidden on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The healing is only a side result of eating, so it is allowed.

steps.title: Why the ruling of רב and שמואל is still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה about שבת would not have taught us that שתיתא needs a ברכה. The ruling of רב and שמואל is therefore necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ruling of רב and שמואל is necessary. If we only had the other source (the משנה about שבת), I would have said that it works only when a person means to eat and the healing comes by itself. But here, he means from the start to use it as medicine, so he should not make a ברכה on it at all. So they teach us that since he enjoys it, he must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question. If אביי's answer already treats שתיתא as food, why do we need רב and שמואל to tell us it gets a ברכה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה on שבת only covers someone who means to eat, with the healing coming on its own. Someone who takes שתיתא mainly as medicine might seem to need no ברכה, just like medicine. רב and שמואל teach that since he still gets הנאה (enjoyment) from it, he must make a ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (the גמרא is explaining why a teaching is not redundant)
I would have thought (the mistaken first idea)
From the start / his main intent

steps.whatToRemember: A ברכה depends on הנאה. Even if you eat something mainly for health, if you enjoy it you make a ברכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for making a ברכה on tasty foods or drinks taken for health reasons.

phrases.english: And the statement of Rav and Shmuel is necessary.
For if only from this (Mishnah), I would have said
(there) he intends to eat
phrases.notes: The case of the משנה about שבת

phrases.english: and the healing comes on its own,
but here, since from the outset
he intends it for healing —
let him not bless over it at all.
It teaches us
that since he has enjoyment from it
he needs to make a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why רב and שמואל's ruling is needed, given אביי's proof from the משנה about שבת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each source teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without רב and שמואל, we would think that food taken mainly as medicine needs no ברכה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the person enjoys it, he must make a ברכה even if his main intent is healing.

steps.title: The wording of the bread blessing: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the ברכה on bread. A ברייתא then records a dispute between the חכמים (״הַמּוֹצִיא״) and רבי נחמיה (״מוֹצִיא״).
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: on bread one says ״הַמּוֹצִיא״. The Rabbis taught: What does he say? ״הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ״. רבי נחמיה says: ״מוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה, the ברכה on bread. It brings a ברייתא that argues over one small word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only difference between the two views is the letter ה at the start of the word. The חכמים say ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ and רבי נחמיה says ״מוֹצִיא״. The next step explains why this one letter matters.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who brings/brought out' with the ה. The opening word of the bread ברכה. Its tense is what the dispute is about.
The same word without the ה. Everyone agrees it means 'brought out' (past tense).
A תנא who disagrees with the חכמים here

phrases.english: (The Mishnah said:) that over bread he says 'Hamotzi', etc.
The Rabbis taught: What does he say? —
'Who brought forth (hamotzi) bread from the earth.'
Rabbi Nechemya says:
'Who brought forth (motzi) bread from the earth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the שתיתא discussion and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים say the ברכה is ״הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ״. רבי נחמיה says ״מוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ״.

steps.title: רבא explains what the dispute is really about
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone agrees ״מוֹצִיא״ means 'brought out' (past). The argument is only over ״הַמּוֹצִיא״: the חכמים say it means past, and רבי נחמיה says it means present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: about ״מוֹצִיא״, everyone agrees it means 'brought out', as it says 'God who brought them out of Egypt'. They argue about ״הַמּוֹצִיא״. The חכמים hold it means 'brought out', as it says 'who brought out water for you from the flint rock'. רבי נחמיה holds it means 'brings out', as it says 'who brings you out from under the burdens of Egypt'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the reason behind the dispute. Both sides want a ברכה about the past, since the bread already came from the ground. They only argue about which word says 'past'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree ״מוֹצִיא״ is past tense, based on a verse. The חכמים prove from another verse that ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ is also past tense, so it is fine to use. רבי נחמיה points to a verse where ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ describes something still happening, so he avoids it.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides want a ברכה in the past tense. The fight is not about past versus present for the ברכה itself. It is only about what the word ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ means.

phrases.english: Rava said:
About 'motzi' everyone agrees
that it means 'brought out' (past),
as it is written: 'God who brought them out of Egypt.'
Where they argue is about 'hamotzi':
the Rabbis hold that 'hamotzi' means 'brought out' (past),
as it is written: 'Who brought out for you water from the flint rock.'
phrases.notes: דברים 8:15, which describes a past event

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה סָבַר הַמּוֹצִיא דְּמַפֵּיק מַשְׁמַע,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Nechemya holds that 'hamotzi' means 'brings out' (present),
as it says: 'Who brings you out from under the burdens of Egypt.'
phrases.notes: שמות 6:7, said while they were still in Egypt

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּ״מוֹצִיא״ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״מוֹצִיא״ is past tense for everyone. The dispute is whether ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ is past tense (חכמים) or present tense (רבי נחמיה).

steps.title: How do the חכמים handle רבי נחמיה's verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים deal with the verse רבי נחמיה brought, where ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ seems to be present tense.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים, how do they explain that verse?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question challenges the חכמים and sets up the next step. It asks what they do with רבי נחמיה's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה's verse was said while the Jews were still in Egypt. That makes ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ look like it means 'is bringing out' right now. The חכמים need to explain why that verse does not hurt their view.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis? (How do they answer this?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? (How do they explain that verse?) —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי נחמיה's proof-verse into a challenge against the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's claim that ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ means past tense
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמות 6:7 uses ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ about a rescue that had not happened yet. That suggests the word is present tense.

steps.title: The חכמים reread the verse as past tense
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים explain that the verse looks to the future. Once God takes them out, they will know He is the One who already brought them out. So ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ there is past tense too.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse means this: הקב"ה said to the Jews, 'When I take you out, I will do something for you so that you will know that I am the One who took you out of Egypt.' As it says: 'And you will know that I am ה׳ your God, who brought you out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the חכמים. It shows that even רבי נחמיה's verse can be read in the past tense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse starts with 'and you will know', which describes later knowledge. At that later time, the leaving of Egypt will already be over. So ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ describes a finished act, and the חכמים's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows the חכמים: we say ״הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ״.

phrases.english: That (verse) means this: said to them
the Holy One, Blessed be He, to Israel:
'When I bring you out,
I will do something for you
so that you will know
that I am the One who brought you out of Egypt,'

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וִידַעְתֶּם כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם הַמּוֹצִיא״.
phrases.english: as it is written: 'And you will know that I am ה׳ your God who brought (you) out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the verse: it describes knowledge after the event
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמות 6:7 uses ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ for something happening now.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse speaks from the time after the Exodus, so ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ there is past tense.

steps.title: A scholar praised as an expert in blessings
steps.stepSummary: A story begins. The חכמים praise the son of רב זביד to רבי זירא as a great man and an expert in ברכות. רבי זירא asks to meet him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים praised to רבי זירא the son of רב זביד, brother of רבי שמואל בר רב זביד, saying he was a great man and an expert in ברכות. רבי זירא said to them: 'When he comes your way, bring him to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to the ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ dispute. This part only sets the scene for what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man is praised as an expert in ברכות. That builds the expectation that he will say the ברכה on bread in the best way. The story will test that praise.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who is the main figure in the story

phrases.english: The Rabbis would praise to Rabbi Zeira
the son of Rav Zevid,

phrases.aramaic: אֲחוּהּ דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב זְבִיד
phrases.english: brother of Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Zevid,
that he is a great man
and he is an expert in blessings.
He (Rabbi Zeira) said to them:
When he comes your way,
bring him to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that tests the ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ / ״מוֹצִיא״ dispute in a real-life case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup: the son of רב זביד has a reputation as an expert in ברכות.

steps.title: The scholar says ״מוֹצִיא״ over bread
steps.stepSummary: The man visits רבי זירא. He is served bread, and he makes the ברכה with ״מוֹצִיא״, the wording everyone agrees is past tense.
steps.simpleTranslation: One time he came to רבי זירא. They brought him bread. He began and said ״מוֹצִיא״.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The scholar makes the ברכה with ״מוֹצִיא״, which sets up רבי זירא's reaction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying ״מוֹצִיא״ is the safe choice. רבא just explained that both the חכמים and רבי נחמיה agree ״מוֹצִיא״ means past tense, so this wording works for both sides. By using it, the scholar avoids taking a side in the dispute, and that is what bothers רבי זירא in the next step.

phrases.english: One time he happened to come to him;
they brought out bread for him;
he began and said 'Motzi.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the scholar's actual ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scholar said ״מוֹצִיא״, the wording everyone agrees is past tense, and so avoided taking a side in the ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ dispute.

steps.title: רבי זירא is disappointed
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא wonders aloud whether this is really the expert in ברכות. He begins to explain what would have been better if the man had said ״הַמּוֹצִיא״. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבי זירא) said: 'Is this the one they say is a great man and an expert in ברכות?! It would make sense if he had said ״הַמּוֹצִיא״...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא objects to the scholar's choice of ״מוֹצִיא״. His reasoning starts here with 'it would make sense if...' and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא is setting up a contrast. Saying ״הַמּוֹצִיא״ would have taken a stand in the dispute and taught something. Saying ״מוֹצִיא״, which everyone already accepts, shows no special expertise. His full reasoning finishes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It would make sense / granted (sets up a contrast)
Is this the one?! (said in surprise)

phrases.english: He said: Is this the one about whom they say

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָדָם גָּדוֹל הוּא וּבָקִי בִּבְרָכוֹת הוּא?!
phrases.english: that he is a great man and an expert in blessings?!
It would make sense if he had said 'Hamotzi'
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הוּא שֶׁאוֹמְרִים עָלָיו דְּאָדָם גָּדוֹל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי זירא reacts critically to the ״מוֹצִיא״ ברכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scholar's reputation as an expert in ברכות, given that he said ״מוֹצִיא״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Had he said ״הַמּוֹצִיא״, he would have shown what that word means and taken a clear stand in the dispute. By saying ״מוֹצִיא״, which everyone already accepts, he showed no special expertise. The full reasoning continues on the next amud.
